title: Lecture 4 — laboratory and lab-kit introduction
summary: The lab kit turns logic diagrams into physical circuits. Reliable work starts with known breadboard connections, correct power and IC orientation, defined inputs, and a repeatable path from schematic to tested evidence.
body:
This lecture introduces the IE1204 lab kit and the practical discipline needed to build digital circuits without damaging components or hiding wiring errors. The central sequence is simple: understand the breadboard, establish safe power and definite input levels, build from a complete schematic, test the circuit, and retain enough evidence to explain what it did.

The scheduled lab workshops support this work. The assessed **LABA laboratory work** is compulsory and includes demonstrations and an individually written report; a timetable entry alone is not evidence that a lab was completed.
